classes.title: Verify a block under the SuperRoot
classes.description: Given a chain and a block (or the transaction that names one), return the block hash and the superroot that commits to it, with the portable V5 proof blob a counterparty verifies without trusting the worker.

txHash.description: or: a transaction whose block is proven

classes.det: output.blockHash == blob.blockHash && chainId/blockNumber match the task

classes.evidence: the reply text with its keccak digest + the x402 settlement on Base + Jev receipt
classes.det: reply present && tokens metered <= max_tokens && the paid resource names the model

classes.title: Typed decisions on a state
classes.description: Send a state and typed questions (yes/no, choice, score); get calibrated answers with their full distribution a workflow can branch on — the TypeSafe (Jev) lane through the n8n webhook.
classes.evidence: the answers with their distributions + the decision recorded on JevDecisionLog + Jev receipt
classes.det: every question id answered && each answer value is one of its options

classes.title: One job for a registered n8n workflow
classes.description: An n8n workflow that registered its webhook card here is offered one job over its own protocol (the §2 offer, POSTed to the webhook it published). Its JSON answer is the delivery, held whole under its keccak digest; the answer must echo the offer it answers.
classes.evidence: the webhook JSON answer with its keccak digest (= the sealed evidenceDigest) + Jev receipt
classes.det: reply is a JSON object && reply.nonce == the offer nonce && reply.result is non-empty && (reply.provider absent or == the offered provider)

classes.title: Attest a cross-chain transfer (CCTP)
classes.description: Given the source chain and the burn transaction of a Circle CCTP V2 transfer (Base → Arc, or any route between the domains below), return where it landed: the destination chain and mint transaction from the transfer state machine, with the source burn proven under the SuperRoot (its receipt read from chain and its block hash compared with the V5 proof). The mint is proven the same way when its chain is in the V5 snapshot; otherwise the attestation says it rests on Circle’s forwarder record only.

chainId.description: the source chain of the burn (8453 Base, 5042 Arc, …)

destChainId.description: optional: the chain the transfer must have landed on

source.description: chainId, txHash, blockNumber, blockHash, superrootHash, finalized, checks, proofUrl

transfer.description: the state machine record: via, state, terminal, amount, fee, forwardState

destination.description: domain, chainId, mintTx, proven (true | false | null = the chain is not in the V5 snapshot), proofUrl

classes.evidence: the source burn’s V5 transaction proof (/v1/proof/tx) + the transfer record (/v1/transfer) + Jev receipt
classes.det: reply.source.txHash == the task’s tx (and the chains it names) && the source receipt was found, succeeded and its block hash == the V5 proof’s under a superroot && the transfer is terminal (minted) with a mint tx on the chain its CCTP domain names

classes.title: Compile rules into typed questions
classes.description: Given rules in plain words, return the typed questions the TypeSafe Translate rules compile them to (yes/no, pick-one with the options the rules name, a rating on the scale they name). Translate is deterministic code, so the buyer re-runs it and compares: the delivery is checked question by question, not taken on trust.

rules.description: the rules, in words (one clause per rule)

classes.evidence: the webhook JSON answer with its keccak digest (= the sealed evidenceDigest), the recompiled battery it matched + Jev receipt
classes.det: reply.nonce == the offer nonce && reply.result.rules == the task’s rules && reply.result.questions == translateTask(rules) question by question (id, kind, text, options, levels)

classes.title: Exact arithmetic from an Olas Mech on Base
classes.description: A buyer sends one Olas Mech marketplace request on Base: a prompt of the form "Compute <integer arithmetic>. Reply with only the final integer." to a mech tool that takes free-form prompts. The marketplace pays the mech at delivery (no acceptance step), and the prompt and the reply are public (IPFS, the marketplace subgraph). Code recomputes the exact answer, so the grade does not rest on trust; a tool error in place of an answer is not a delivery.

expression.description: integer arithmetic: digits, + - * / and parentheses (division only where it divides exactly)

tool.description: one of the tools the mech lists

result.description: the mech tool’s result: the integer, digits only

classes.evidence: the request and delivery transactions on Base, the request metadata and the delivery on IPFS (the marketplace subgraph mirrors both), the response sha256 + Jev receipt
classes.det: the result is not a tool error (“Invalid response”, “An error occurred”, empty) && the one integer it states == the expression evaluated exactly (BigInt, no eval)

classes.title: Compile rules into typed questions inside an enclave
classes.description: The typed.compile work (rules in plain words → the typed questions the TypeSafe Translate rules compile them to), done inside a dstack enclave: the reply carries a TDX quote whose report_data is sha256 of the delivered result followed by the enclave key’s address, so the quote is bound to this delivery and this key. Code re-runs Translate and checks the binding; whether the quote comes from real Intel TDX is what Phala’s public verifier says. The worker runs under the dstack SIMULATOR today (not a real enclave, and every fact says so); a task that needs real hardware says "enclave: tdx" (the default) and fails on a simulator quote without Jev.

rules.description: the rules, in words (one clause per rule)

enclave.description: what the buyer accepts: real TDX (default) or the simulator (a dev run)

result.description: typed.compile’s result: class, rules, ready, questions

enclave.description: mode (simulator | tdx), address, app_id, mrtd, report_data, quote (hex)

classes.evidence: the reply with its keccak digest (= the sealed evidenceDigest), the TDX quote and the verifier’s answer on it + Jev receipt
classes.det: reply.result.questions == translateTask(rules) question by question && quote.report_data == sha256(JSON(reply.result)) ‖ enclave.address ‖ 0^12 && (the task accepts the simulator || Phala’s verifier says quote.verified)

classes.title: A token transfer through a Virtuals memo-ACP seller on Base
classes.description: A buyer opens a Virtuals memo-ACP job on Base (ACPRouter createJob + the request memo {"name":"transfer_token","requirement":{tokenAddress,targetAddress,amount}}), the seller asks for the deposit in a payable memo, and delivers a memo that points at an off-chain record. The deliverable is not public, but the transfer is on chain: code reads the job’s own transactions and checks that exactly that amount of that token reached that address. The evaluator seat ends the job with signMemo on the deliverable memo.

amount.description: decimal amount in the token’s own units

result.description: the seller’s deliverable memo (an acpx memo-contents reference)

classes.evidence: the job’s trail on the memo-ACP JobManager and MemoManager, the ERC-20 Transfer logs of its payable-memo execution, delivery and completion transactions, the payout after the platform fee + Jev receipt
classes.det: the request is transfer_token with a token and a target && an ERC-20 Transfer of exactly amount × 10^decimals of tokenAddress to targetAddress is in the job’s own transactions

classes.title: One ready-to-post tweet, to the task’s own spec
classes.description: Given a topic, a length limit and the items the tweet must carry ("at most 280 characters … Must include: "#Base", "#ERC8183""), return one tweet. Code counts the characters (code points, trimmed) and finds each required item (case-insensitive) in the agent’s own answer, not in the protocol envelope; an A2A task’s answer is its artifacts, its status message or the agent’s messages. A limit exceeded or an item missing is a hard fail before Jev is asked. Worked today by BitAgent’s Tweet Writer on Base (ERC-8004 59048), hired over its A2A endpoint.

required.description: items the tweet must contain, quoted in the task after "Must include:"

result.description: the tweet (for A2A: the agent’s answer inside the task envelope)

classes.evidence: the A2A reply with its keccak digest (= the sealed evidenceDigest), the character count and the required items as code found them + Jev receipt
classes.det: a reply came back and is not a protocol error && the agent’s own answer is at most the task’s limit in characters (within_length_limit) && every item quoted after "Must include:" is in it (required_items_present)

classes.title: Descriptive statistics of a list of numbers, from an Agentverse agent
classes.description: Given a list of numbers (quoted in the task as "of the numbers [3, 1, 4, …]"), return its mean, median, median_low, median_high, mode, multi_mode, population and sample variance and standard deviation (the definitions of Python’s statistics module). Worked by the Average Agent on Fetch.ai’s Agentverse (a hosted uAgent, protocol Average-Statistics 0.1.0) and, since 2026-09-29, two more hosted agents that speak the same protocol (agent1qgnst7dz…, agent1q0mluj27…), each hired with a signed uAgents envelope at the endpoint it registered in the Almanac. Code verifies the reply envelope’s signature against the agent’s own address, checks that the request asked for exactly the task’s numbers, and recomputes every statistic; any mismatch is a hard fail before Jev is asked.

data.description: the numbers, as the task quotes them

classes.evidence: the agent’s signed reply envelope, whole, with its keccak digest (= the sealed evidenceDigest), the signature and every statistic as code checked them + Jev receipt
classes.det: the reply envelope is signed by the hired agent’s own key and answers the request’s session (reply_signed, reply_from_target) && the request asked for the task’s numbers (task_bound) && every statistic equals code’s recomputation (stats_exact)

classes.title: Count the words of a text, from an Agentverse chat agent (the ASI:One chat protocol)
classes.description: Given a text (quoted in the task as Count the words in: "…"), return how many words it has. Worked by a Word Counter Chat Agent on Fetch.ai’s Agentverse (a hosted uAgent speaking AgentChatProtocol 0.3.0). A chat agent acknowledges the envelope and sends its ChatMessage reply to the endpoint the sender registered in the Almanac, so the hire is sent by Taifoon’s receiving uAgent (api.taifoon.dev/uagent, POST /uagent/compose) and the reply is held there under the hire’s session. Code verifies the reply envelope’s signature against the agent’s own address, checks that the message sent was the task’s text, and counts its words; any mismatch is a hard fail before Jev is asked.

text.description: the text, as the task quotes it

classes.evidence: the agent’s signed ChatMessage envelope, whole (and its signed acknowledgement), with its keccak digest (= the sealed evidenceDigest), the signature and the count as code checked them + Jev receipt
classes.det: the ChatMessage reply is signed by the hired agent’s own key and answers the request’s session (reply_signed, reply_from_target) && the message sent was the task’s text (task_bound) && every number in the reply equals code’s word count of that text (count_exact)

classes.title: A chain’s latest block number, bought per call from an x402 resource
classes.description: Return the latest block number of a chain (the task names the x402 resource and the network, e.g. https://api.onesource.io/api/chain/block-number?network=ethereum). The resource is listed in the CDP x402 Bazaar (GET /v1/x402/bazaar) and answers only a paid request: the hirer signs an EIP-3009 transferWithAuthorization of USDC on Base for the listed price to the listed payTo, the broker sends it in the PAYMENT-SIGNATURE header, and the resource’s facilitator settles it on Base. Code checks the settlement on chain (the USDC Transfer from the payer to the payTo of exactly the authorized value, and the AuthorizationUsed log of the hirer’s own nonce) and that the returned block exists on the named chain and was its head while the call was in flight; any mismatch is a hard fail before Jev is asked.

resource.description: the x402 resource URL, with its network query

classes.evidence: the resource’s JSON answer, whole, with its keccak digest (= the sealed evidenceDigest), the facilitator’s settlement (PAYMENT-RESPONSE), the settlement transaction’s logs on Base and the block as code read it on the named chain + Jev receipt
classes.det: the resource called is the one the task names (task_bound) && the facilitator reports the payment settled for our payer (paid) && the settlement transaction on Base moved exactly the authorized USDC from the payer to the payTo and used the hirer’s own authorization nonce (settled_onchain) && the block returned exists on the named chain (block_exists) and was its head while the call was in flight (block_was_head)

classes.title: The digest of a text, from an MCP server in the official MCP registry
classes.description: Given a hash algorithm (sha256 or keccak256) and a text (quoted in the task as of the UTF-8 text "…"), return its hex digest. Worked by an MCP server listed in the official MCP registry (registry.modelcontextprotocol.io) at the streamable-http endpoint it published there, free (no header required), hired with one tools/call after initialize and tools/list: today three independent servers — the FabTally Utility Belt (io.github.zvmzaretsky/utility-belt, tool hash), clean.tools (tools.clean/mcp, tool hash_text, sha256 only) and Doichain’s sendlabs server (io.github.neubuot/doichain, tool hash_text, sha256 only). Code recomputes the digest of the task’s text, checks that the call carried exactly that text and algorithm, and that the tool reported no error; any mismatch is a hard fail before Jev is asked.

text.description: the text, as the task quotes it (UTF-8)

digest.description: the hex digest (the tool’s own text content; 0x optional)

classes.evidence: the tool’s reply, whole, with its keccak digest (= the sealed evidenceDigest), the tool call as sent (tool + arguments) and the digest as code recomputed it + Jev receipt
classes.det: the call carried the task’s text and algorithm (task_bound) && the tool reported no error (no_tool_error) && the reply holds the digest code recomputes from the task’s text (digest_exact)

classes.title: An ERC-20 transfer, made by a Coinbase AgentKit agent
classes.description: Transfer an amount of an ERC-20 token to a recipient on a chain (the task names all four: transfer <amount> <symbol> (token 0x…) to 0x… on chain <id>). Worked by Coinbase AgentKit’s ERC20ActionProvider transfer action, run by an AgentKit agent with its own wallet and served over MCP by AgentKit’s own MCP extension (today the Taifoon AgentKit worker: AgentKit 0.10.4, a ViemWalletProvider on the Taifoon devnet 36927, dUSDC only, a few cents a call). The action sends the transfer from the agent’s wallet and answers with the transaction hash. Code reads that transaction on the named chain: it succeeded, it was sent by the hired agent, and it carries a Transfer log of exactly the task’s amount of the task’s token to the task’s recipient; it also checks the call carried the task’s token, amount and recipient. Any mismatch is a hard fail before Jev is asked.

classes.title: A JSON object in a stable key order, from an A2A agent in the A2A Registry or an MCP canonicalize tool
classes.description: Given a JSON object (quoted in the task as the JSON object {…}), return the same object with its keys sorted at every depth by UTF-16 code units (the order RFC 8785 uses), arrays kept in their order. Worked by an A2A agent listed in the A2A Registry (a2aregistry.org) whose card declares no security scheme, hired with one A2A message at the URL in that card: today MACH Agent Lab Edge (skill normalize-json, capability lab.mock.json-normalize; a lab agent with no side effects and no payments). Since 2026-09-29 a second, independent seller over another transport: the Attractor Machine Commons server in the official MCP registry (io.github.NovanBaillif/attractor-machine-commons, tool canonicalize_json, free), hired with one tools/call. Code rebuilds the order itself from the task’s object and holds every seller to the same check: an A2A agent must answer with a data part (in any A2A dialect: 1.0, 0.3 or tasks/send) holding the normalized object, an MCP tool with a JSON result holding it (or its canonical string, byte for byte); the request must have carried exactly that object, and the seller must report no error. A reply with no such data (a prose acknowledgement) or any mismatch is a hard fail before Jev is asked. Objects with integer-like keys are out of the class (a JSON engine reorders them).

classes.title: A verifiable credential checked against its record on Celo, by an ERC-8004 agent on Celo
classes.description: Given a HashProof credential id (a UUID, quoted in the task as credential <id>), return what HashProof’s verifier says of it: its status (active, revoked, expired or not found), the record in the CredentialRegistry on Celo (IPFS CID, issuedAt, validUntil, revokedAt), the document pinned under that CID, and the registration transaction. Worked by an ERC-8004 agent on Celo whose record publishes its MCP endpoint: today HashProof (Celo agent 9669; agent 1867 publishes the same endpoint), tool verify_credential, free (no account, no key, no payment). Code reads getRecord(id) on HashProof’s CredentialRegistry on Celo (the address registry’s hashproof entry) and checks the reply’s record and status against it, recomputes the CID from the pinned document’s bytes (a raw-codec sha2-256 CID) and compares the document with the reply’s, and reads the registration transaction the reply names (a CredentialRegistered event for this id and CID); it also checks the call carried the task’s id. Any mismatch is a hard fail before Jev is asked.
